stories.summary: Restore the app.dashboard package attribute when the fresh_import fixture ends
stories.description: A test-only fixture leak made test_dashboard_save_route_answers_403_for_a_refused_caller fail intermittently with 400 instead of 403 on two unrelated branches.
stories.agent_instructions:
Preflight: impact run 2026-10-28 on master e965e7b - all four stories applied as stand-ins in one scratch worktree: 18062 passed -> 18139 passed / 17 skipped, 0 conflicts, ruff and check_line_limit clean, pin-guard baseline green. The only adjustment needed was import ordering in the fixture stand-in (ruff I001), fixed in place.
TARGET IMPLEMENTER: cloud open-source (Claude-class sizing, every mechanically checkable requirement graded below). Provider/model are NOT pinned: dispatch resolves them from the live model registry's `roles.dispatch` entry.

ROOT CAUSE (measured 2026-10-28, not guessed): tests/unit/test_dashboard_preflight_log.py's `fresh_import` fixture pops `sys.modules["app.dashboard"]`, imports a fresh module - which rebinds the `app` package's `dashboard` attribute to that fresh module - and then restores only `sys.modules`. The package attribute stays bound to the discarded module. Any later test in the same pytest-xdist worker that patches `from app import dashboard as d; d._service.save_plan` therefore patches the discarded module, while `app.dashboard_routes_plan._dashboard()` resolves the original module from `sys.modules`, so the REAL PipelineService runs. In tests/unit/test_plan_authoring_enforcement.py::test_dashboard_save_route_answers_403_for_a_refused_caller the real service parses `not-json{` and answers 400 instead of the expected 403. Whether the two modules disagree depends on which tests share a worker, which is why it appeared on two unrelated branches (agent/lg-03, agent/br-01) and vanished after a rebase.

WHAT TO DO (test-only; no production change):
1. In tests/unit/test_dashboard_preflight_log.py, make the fixture restore BOTH `sys.modules[DASHBOARD_MODULE]` and the `app` package's `dashboard` attribute to what they were before the yield. Capture `saved_attribute = vars(app).get("dashboard", _ABSENT)` with a module-level `_ABSENT = object()` sentinel before the yield; after it, restore `sys.modules` as today, then set `app.dashboard = saved_attribute`, or `vars(app).pop("dashboard", None)` when it was absent. Add `import app` to the imports (ruff will want it sorted). Keep the docstring accurate: it now restores both bindings.
2. Do NOT change app/dashboard_routes_plan.py, app/dashboard.py, or pipeline/*. The defect is the fixture leaving global state inconsistent, not the route's resolution.
3. Add one regression test in the same file: after the fresh-import window closes, `app.dashboard` and `sys.modules["app.dashboard"]` are the same object again, and patching `app.dashboard._service.save_plan` reaches `app.dashboard_routes_plan._service.save_plan` (assert identity through the route module's proxy).

DONE WHEN: the new regression test fails on master's fixture (restore is incomplete) and passes after the fix; `git diff --stat master` shows only test files; full suite, ruff and check_line_limit are green.

- Verify with the full suite `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` AND `.venv/bin/python -m ruff check .` AND `.venv/bin/python scripts/check_line_limit.py`; all must be green before you finish. Report pass/fail counts in the PR description.

stories.summary: Remove the release-ordering race from the store transaction contract test
stories.description: test_transaction_mutual_exclusion_across_threads failed on master's own CI because the third holder starts acquiring before the first has released.
stories.agent_instructions:
Preflight: impact run 2026-10-28 on master e965e7b - all four stories applied as stand-ins in one scratch worktree: 18062 passed -> 18139 passed / 17 skipped, 0 conflicts, ruff and check_line_limit clean, pin-guard baseline green. The only adjustment needed was import ordering in the fixture stand-in (ruff I001), fixed in place.
TARGET IMPLEMENTER: cloud open-source (Claude-class sizing, every mechanically checkable requirement graded below). Provider/model are NOT pinned: dispatch resolves them from the live model registry's `roles.dispatch` entry.

ROOT CAUSE (measured 2026-10-28): in tests/contract/test_store_contract.py::test_transaction_mutual_exclusion_across_threads, `contender_b` sets `b_checked` in its `finally` *while `holder_a` still holds the lock*, and `holder_c` starts acquiring as soon as `b_checked` is set. Nothing orders C's acquire after A's release, so on a loaded runner C can lose the race and fail `assert acquired is True, "the lock must be free after the holder releases"`. This failed master's own CI run 40741252758 (Python 3.11) and an ENF-03 run, and passed 40/40 in a local loop.

WHAT TO DO (test-only; production code is correct):
1. Add `a_released = threading.Event()` next to the other events.
2. In `holder_a`, set `a_released.set()` AFTER the `with store.transaction(PLAN)` block exits (the lock is released when the context manager exits; setting it inside would reintroduce the race).
3. In `holder_c`, wait on `a_released` ("the holder never released") instead of `b_checked`. Every assertion stays exactly as it is - this fixes the ordering, it does not loosen the test. `b_checked` is still what `holder_a` waits on, which is what proves B's refused attempt did not clobber A's lock.
4. Keep the docstring accurate: it describes the A->B->C->D handoff, so mention that C waits for A's release.

DONE WHEN: the test passes in a loop (`for i in $(seq 1 25); do .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q "tests/contract/test_store_contract.py::test_transaction_mutual_exclusion_across_threads"; done`), no assertion was weakened or removed, and the full suite, ruff and check_line_limit are green.

stories.summary: Assert the login callback redirects to the validated next path
stories.description: LG-03 stored the validated next on the pending login and redirects to it in _finish_login, but no test exercises that last hop.
stories.agent_instructions:

WHY: tests/unit/test_oidc_login_next.py proves `validate_next_path` rejects the open-redirect shapes and that `/auth/login` stores the validated value on `_PendingLogin.next`. Nothing proves `_finish_login` redirects to that stored value rather than to `/` - so a regression there would pass the whole suite while silently dropping the return-to-page behaviour.

WHAT TO DO (one new test; no production change expected):
1. Add the test to tests/unit/test_oidc_login_flow.py, reusing that file's existing `_FakeIdP` fixture and monkeypatch seams (`oidc_login._fetch_json`, `oidc_login._post_form`, `oidc_login._now`) rather than inventing a second fake. Adding cases to an existing test file needs no approval; do not modify or weaken any existing test in it.
2. Drive `/auth/login?next=/plans/x?tab=2`, take the minted `state` from the redirect Location, then complete `/auth/callback?code=...&state=...` through the fake provider, and assert the response is a 302 whose Location is exactly `/plans/x?tab=2`, and that the session cookie was set.
3. Second case: `/auth/login?next=//evil.example` then the same callback, asserting the Location is `/`. That is the end-to-end proof of the open-redirect guard.
4. If and only if `_finish_login` does NOT redirect to `pending.next`, that is a real defect: fix it in app/oidc_login_routes.py (the file is declared for exactly that reason) and say so in the commit body.

DONE WHEN: both new tests fail when `_finish_login` is temporarily changed to `RedirectResponse("/")` (verify by making that edit locally and reverting it), and the full suite, ruff and check_line_limit are green.

stories.summary: Replace the main.js whole-file hash pin with a durable wiring assertion
stories.description: test_comms_landing_redesign.py pins main.js's whole-file SHA-256, which eight unrelated stories have had to re-pin.
stories.agent_instructions:
Preflight: impact run 2026-10-28 on master e965e7b - all four stories applied as stand-ins in one scratch worktree: 18062 passed -> 18139 passed / 17 skipped, 0 conflicts, ruff and check_line_limit clean, pin-guard baseline green. WHY: tests/unit/test_comms_landing_redesign.py keeps `_UNCHANGED_JS_SHA256[MAIN_JS]`, a whole-file digest of static/app/main.js, asserted by `test_main_js_untouched`. `git log -G'MAIN_JS'` shows eight separate stories re-pinning it, the most recent being LG-03, because main.js is the dashboard's main script and every UI story legitimately edits it. A byte hash cannot distinguish 'this story drifted' from 'the next story did its job', and the repo's pin-guard policy says a self-guard must never pin a file a later sibling is scheduled to edit.

WHAT TO DO (test-only):
1. In tests/unit/test_comms_landing_redesign.py, delete the `MAIN_JS` entry (and its accumulated re-pin comment block) from `_UNCHANGED_JS_SHA256`, keeping the `APP_JS` entry and its comment untouched.
2. Replace `test_main_js_untouched` with `test_main_js_keeps_the_comms_landing_wiring`, asserting only durable anchors that this story's sibling stories must not remove: main.js still imports `renderToolTraceHtml, appendCommsMessage, sendCommsMessage, updateCommsSubtitle, resetCommsThread` from `"./comms.js"`; it still calls `updateCommsSubtitle();`; and it still re-exports `resetCommsThread,`. Assert membership/substrings, never a digest or a count of the whole file.
3. Update tests/unit/pin_guard_baseline.json: the entry `"tests/unit/test_comms_landing_redesign.py": [30, 86]` becomes `[30]` (the baseline is shrink-only; a stale entry fails the pin-guard test). Re-measure the remaining line number after your edit - if the `APP_JS` pin moved, record its new line instead.

DONE WHEN: `grep -c "sha256" tests/unit/test_comms_landing_redesign.py` shows no pin of main.js; the new test fails if someone removes the `updateCommsSubtitle();` call (verify locally, then revert); test_pin_guard_baseline.py, the full suite, ruff and check_line_limit are green.
